name: Video Games
one_liner: Developers, publishers, and platforms monetizing interactive entertainment, a hit-driven business increasingly built on live services and in-game spending.
how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from full-price game sales, in-game purchases in free-to-play and live-service titles, subscriptions such as Game Pass, and platform fees on third-party sales. Console makers often sell hardware near cost and profit from software royalties and digital store commissions.
revenue_formula: Premium revenue = units sold × average net price
cost_structure: Development: large teams and multi-year cycles, with AAA budgets rising sharply
Marketing and user acquisition: especially heavy for mobile games
Platform fees: storefronts commonly take ~30% of digital sales
Live operations: servers, content updates, and community management
margins: Operating margins vary widely, from losses for failed titles to roughly 25-35%+ for publishers with hit franchises and live services. Franchise strength, live-service engagement, and platform-fee exposure drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Daily / monthly active users (DAU/MAU)
key_metrics.what: Size and stickiness of the player base; the foundation of live-service revenue.

key_metrics.name: ARPDAU / ARPPU
key_metrics.what: Revenue per daily active user or per paying user; measures monetization depth.

key_metrics.name: Payer conversion
key_metrics.what: Share of players who spend money; often a small minority in free-to-play.

key_metrics.name: Retention (D1/D7/D30)
key_metrics.what: Share of new players still active after 1, 7, or 30 days; predicts lifetime value.

key_metrics.name: Net bookings
key_metrics.what: Sales and in-game spending before deferral accounting; the industry's preferred top line.

key_metrics.name: Player acquisition cost (CPI)
key_metrics.what: Cost to acquire an installed player; must be below lifetime value.

trends: Consolidation and acquisitions of major publishers alongside widespread layoffs and studio closures
Rising AAA development costs pushing publishers toward proven franchises and live services
Challenges to app-store fees opening alternative payment and distribution routes on mobile
Subscription and cross-platform play spreading across console, PC, and mobile
Generative AI tools entering asset creation and game development
Platforms like Roblox and Fortnite growing user-generated content economies

case_angles.question: A publisher's flagship live-service game is losing players; how do we restore revenue?
Should a console maker launch its games on PC and mobile?
How should a free-to-play game design its pricing and in-game store?
Should a large publisher acquire a mobile game studio?

interview_hooks: Are 30% platform fees justified, and will regulation break them?
Is the future of gaming subscriptions, free-to-play, or premium releases?
Can AI meaningfully reduce the cost and risk of AAA development?
